requirement.why: Critical infrastructure-layer bug. User cannot see asynchronous claude output without manually 'kicking' the UI. Reduces app to polling-by-user-action.

root_cause_analysis.symptom: Agent text emitted by claude in response to a <task-notification> system-reminder is not rendered in happy-app in real-time; only renders after user sends a new prompt
root_cause_analysis.root_cause: UNCONFIRMED — four candidate hypotheses (H_A app-side seq fast-path miss / H_B InvalidateSync debouncing / H_C ws transport loss / H_D silent flushOutbox backoff). Dev MUST rule in/out at least 2 of 4 via runtime evidence before claiming root cause.
root_cause_analysis.root_cause_commit: candidate: 5a08be71 fix: batch outbox flush (latest-first) and log backoff errors — introduced non-monotonic seq vs logical-time ordering which may starve the app's fast-path
root_cause_analysis.why_introduced: 5a08be71 fixed a 400+-message resume blocking issue by sending newest 50 first to give user fast feedback
root_cause_analysis.why_problematic: Non-monotonic seq order may cause the app's fast-path (incomingSeq === currentLastSeq + 1) to fail repeatedly, falling back to getMessagesSync.invalidate() which may be debounced/coalesced — net effect: passive in-turn updates queue until something invalidates the cache (user sending a message).
root_cause_analysis.timeline: 5a08be71 landed 2026-03-24. cca7fe27 (Bug #9 app seq-gap) landed 2026-03-18 BEFORE 5a08be71. So Bug #9's fix preceded the latest-first batching that may now defeat it. The current symptom likely surfaced sometime between 2026-03-24 and 2026-04-25 but no specific commit between is identified as the regression marker.
